findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses independent booleans and a string to model a lifecycle that requires an explicit state machine. There is no typestate enforcing valid transitions (e.g., you can set is_sent=true while status="pending" or mark both is_validated and is_sent true without ordering).
findings.failure_mode: Programmer can construct or mutate LedgerWorkflow into any invalid combination of lifecycle flags, violating the domain invariant that validation and sending are ordered transitions.
findings.fix: Replace `is_validated: bool`, `is_sent: bool`, and `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` with a single `LedgerStatus` enum with ordered variants like `New`, `Validated`, `Sent(u64)`. Remove `is_validated` and `is_sent` entirely.

findings.problem: `status: String` is a raw string field that accepts any value. `mark_sent` sets it to `"sent"` by string assignment (line 10), which is a magic-string mutation rather than a typed transition. Any caller can set status to an arbitrary string.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid domain states like status="" or status="deleted" are representable. String comparison in callers is fragile. `"sent".to_string()` allocates every call instead of using a zero-cost enum discriminant.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with `status: LedgerStatus` enum. Update `mark_sent` signature to `pub fn mark_sent(item: LedgerWorkflow) -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, LedgerError>` returning `LedgerStatus::Sent` variant instead of mutating a string.

findings.problem: `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` (line 5) encode lifecycle state as independent booleans. This permits impossible combinations (both true, neither true, sent without validated) and provides no transition enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Any of 4 boolean combinations is representable including semantically invalid ones. No ordering constraint between validation and sending is enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Collapse into a single typestate enum: `enum LedgerStatus { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`. Remove both boolean fields and the Option field.

findings.problem: `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` is a top-level optional field that can be `Some(ms)` while `is_sent` is `false`, or `None` while `is_sent` is `true`. The Option does not track which lifecycle state owns it.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid states where the timestamp exists but the item is not marked sent (stale data), or item is marked sent without a timestamp (missing required data). The Option is disconnected from the boolean lifecycle flags it semantically belongs to.
findings.fix: Move the timestamp into the typestate enum variant: `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`. This makes it impossible for the timestamp to exist without the sent state and vice versa.

findings.problem: `id: String` is a raw primitive that carries no domain rules. Any string, empty string, or non-identifier value is accepted. No validation, uniqueness guarantee, or domain semantics are encoded.
findings.failure_mode: Empty IDs, duplicate IDs, or non-unique identifiers are representable. Callers cannot distinguish a `LedgerWorkflow` ID from any other string, enabling mix-ups at API boundaries.
findings.fix: Replace with a newtype: `pub struct LedgerId(String);` with a smart constructor `LedgerId::parse(raw: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError>` that validates non-empty and format. Use `id: LedgerId` in the struct.

findings.problem: `mark_sent` takes `LedgerWorkflow` directly with all raw primitives (`String`, `bool`, `Option<u64>`). There is no parse boundary — raw primitives cross into the domain without fallible smart constructors. Any caller can construct `LedgerWorkflow` with invalid values.
findings.failure_mode: The domain core accepts unvalidated input. Callers can bypass all domain invariants by constructing `LedgerWorkflow` directly with arbitrary field values. The parse boundary is absent so invalid states are not caught at the shell boundary.
findings.fix: Define shell DTO types with raw fields. Implement fallible smart constructors (`LedgerWorkflow::parse(id: &str) -> Result<Self, ...>`) that validate and produce trusted domain types. The core API (`mark_sent`) consumes validated domain values.

residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run, no runtime analysis, no property tests. All six findings are BLOCKER-level typestate/domain-model violations that make illegal states representable. The struct accepts any combination of raw primitives with zero domain invariants enforced by types.
